reviews.comment: Dr. Bapst is a great professor, he's a dinosaur nerd which is a positive aspect for this class, he takes late homework with no penalty, the homework is alright, not a lot, I don't understand the complaints, just do the work and you will be fine, the only downside is the constant team projects that are always a headache online (they're 30% of grade)

Taking this class online was an awesome decision, the lectures were interesting and clear, so were the assignments and labs that went along with them. You will need to put in time and work to get a good grade, but you'll retain so much info. You can tell he is very passionate about this subject, and that enthusiasm makes lectures better.

Heavy workload makes it hard to keep up with other classes. Questions often don't get clear answers, leaving confusion about whether I'm learning correctly. TA grading is strict and feedback is unclear. Katherine Bober was helpful and fair, while Nancy Martinez was much harder to get explanations from and stricter in grading.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course was the worst I have taken in my entire undergrad. Dr. Bapst is not very understanding of medical issues, and this became a big issue for multiple other classmates I talked to during the course. I had to do about 12+ hours of work a week for this course to receive an A. I highly recommend finding another online course/professor.

Dr. Bapst was a good prof, and the class was interesting. The readings were fine, the labs are once a week and were not too hard to figure out, and then there is a few mini assignments throughout the week that are fine as well. Group projects were like labs, time-consuming but manageable. No exams whatsoever.

This is one of the most time consuming and difficult courses I have EVER taken. Do not take this class if you aren't able to put in at least 5 hours of work per week to research dinosaurs. You don't know your grade ever, because grades aren't put in for at least 4 weeks from when assignments are due. Lectures are unhelpful and you are on your own.

This proffesor is genuinely the most awful person. He does not give out any grade until maybe a month after you have turned it in so you have no idea how you are doing in his class. I am a business major and am taking this for a life and physical science but god that was the worst choice. The videos to help you do work make no sense.

This class (Dinosaur World) was the first B I had in my entire life LOL! He gave back 3/4 major assignments AFTER the deadline to submit any more work. He took off major points from our group projects on small things. His TA told me if I turned in my work I would basically get an A, which was wrong. I would not recommend this class.

This was probably the most time consuming class I'll take at A&M. Quizzes and labs every week multiple times a week which aren't super bad there's just a ton of them. You won't know your grades ever as 50% of my grade wasn't even in when grades were supposed to be due. Major assignment due Feb. 21 that wasn't in when grades were due in May.

Dr. Bapst is a good professor and likes the topic, but the problem is transparency. He doesn't let you see your own grades, you have to ask him and he decides if he tells you or not based on what your grade is. You never know what your grade really is and it causes so much confusion grading wise. I wish he was more transparent!

Screw this guy. Why are you teaching college students about dinosaurs in the first place? He hasn't showered in years. I had a 97 with 3 weeks to go and his stuff wasn't that hard but I always was emailing asking what my grade was. He decided to not respond to my email until grades were due telling me I had 88 and I couldn't do anything.

The professor seems very passionate about the subject, which is great. There is a ton of busy work, several assignments a week, that aren't hard to do if you watch the lectures, there is so many. Everything is scheduled to keep you on task and have everything ready by the time group projects roll around. Easily understandable class.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: While the professor isn't a bad teacher there are tons of lectures and assignments. He does however not list all assignments that will be done in the class. Also releases new assignments the week before they are due in batches of at least 5 if not more. You may think you are done with assignments but check again cause I can assure you you are not.

Easy A, no exams. Professor Bapst himself treated students very poorly and punished my group because we worked without one of our assigned group members who was too lazy to communicate with us or help us with the actual work. He refused to hear our side of the story and punished us for "trying to make the group work optional," which was false.
Very unclear about class expectations. Will have no idea where you sand in class (can be anywhere between A and F).
attendance counts, he has weekly ecampus and/or in class assingments. Very harsh grader. Not clear when he assigns work and he is very soft spoken.
